name: Three-Act Structure
description: The classic three-act screenplay structure: Setup, Confrontation, Resolution.

beats.title: Opening Image
beats.description: The very first impression of the story. A single scene or shot that sets the tone, mood, and stakes. It's the 'before' snapshot of the protagonist's world.

beats.title: Exposition / Setup
beats.description: Introduce the protagonist, their world, their routine, and their core flaw or need. Establish the status quo that will be disrupted. Plant seeds for subplots.

beats.title: Inciting Incident
beats.description: The event that disrupts the protagonist's ordinary world and sets the central conflict in motion. Something happens that demands a response.

beats.title: Debate / Refusal
beats.description: The protagonist hesitates. They weigh the cost of action vs. inaction. Internal and external forces push and pull. Stakes are clarified.

beats.title: End of Act One / Plot Point 1
beats.description: The protagonist makes a decisive choice that launches them into the main conflict. There's no turning back. The story shifts into a new direction entirely.

beats.title: Rising Action / Tests & Allies
beats.description: The protagonist navigates the new world of Act 2. They encounter allies, enemies, and obstacles. Subplots develop. The protagonist learns new skills or truths.

beats.title: Midpoint
beats.description: A major revelation, reversal, or escalation at the story's center. Either a false victory (things seem great but won't last) or a false defeat (things seem hopeless but a path will emerge). Raises the stakes dramatically.

beats.title: Complications / Escalation
beats.description: The antagonist closes in. Allies are tested or lost. The protagonist's plan starts to unravel. Pressure intensifies. Subplots converge.

beats.title: Crisis / All Is Lost
beats.description: The protagonist's lowest point. Their plan has failed, their allies are scattered, and the antagonist seems unstoppable. A death (literal or metaphorical) occurs.

beats.title: End of Act Two / Plot Point 2
beats.description: A new piece of information, a renewed determination, or an unexpected ally gives the protagonist a final chance. They commit fully to the climactic confrontation.

beats.title: Climax
beats.description: The final confrontation between protagonist and antagonist. All themes, subplots, and character arcs converge. The protagonist must use everything they've learned.

beats.title: Resolution / Denouement
beats.description: The aftermath. Show the new status quo. Resolve remaining subplots. Demonstrate how the protagonist has changed. The 'after' image contrasting the opening.
